ocr.notes: Mostly right; a few garbled words ('no semeee' for 'no remedy', 'peas ay Geqeee' for 'people are disgusted', McCoole's name dropped from the Commercial quote).

title.suggested: Allen-McCoole Fight Draws Little Interest in St. Louis

summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat reported little St. Louis interest in the November 10 Allen-McCoole fight after Allen's last two disputed fights, while Cincinnati was eager; Jim Coyne held a levee at Allen's saloon.

metadata.notes: The masthead reads 'Daily Democrat, Tuesday Morning, November 2, 1869.'

facts.fact: Allen's second fight with Mike McCoole was set for November 10, 1869, within fifty miles of Cincinnati
Allen was to have had a benefit at Mozart Hall in Cincinnati on October 30, 1869

notes: The paper says the 'unfairness' of Allen's last two fights (with McCoole and Gallagher) made St. Louis suspicious of prize fighting; the Cincinnati Commercial is quoted as saying Allen fairly won both. Coyne was preparing for a fight with Patsey Reardon. 'was to have had a benefit' leaves unclear whether it took place.
